1.sahih_international: By the star when it descends,
1.pickthall: By the Star when it setteth,
1.yusuf_ali: By the Star when it goes down,-
1.shakir: I swear by the star when it goes down.
1.mohsin_khan: By the star when it goes down, (or vanishes).
1.arberry: By the Star when it plunges,

2.sahih_international: Your companion [Muhammad] has not strayed, nor has he erred,
2.pickthall: Your comrade erreth not, nor is deceived;
2.yusuf_ali: Your Companion is neither astray nor being misled.
2.shakir: Your companion does not err, nor does he go astray;
2.muhammad_sarwar: your companion is not in error nor has he gone astray.
2.mohsin_khan: Your companion (Muhammad SAW) has neither gone astray nor has erred.
2.arberry: your comrade is not astray, neither errs,

3.sahih_international: Nor does he speak from [his own] inclination.
3.pickthall: Nor doth he speak of (his own) desire.
3.yusuf_ali: Nor does he say (aught) of (his own) Desire.
3.shakir: Nor does he speak out of desire.
3.muhammad_sarwar: He does not speak out of his own desires.
3.mohsin_khan: Nor does he speak of (his own) desire.
3.arberry: nor speaks he out of caprice.

4.sahih_international: It is not but a revelation revealed,
4.pickthall: It is naught save an inspiration that is inspired,
4.yusuf_ali: It is no less than inspiration sent down to him:
4.shakir: It is naught but revelation that is revealed,
4.muhammad_sarwar: It is a revelations which has been revealed to him
4.mohsin_khan: It is only an Inspiration that is inspired.
4.arberry: This is naught but a revelation revealed,

5.sahih_international: Taught to him by one intense in strength -
5.pickthall: Which one of mighty powers hath taught him,
5.yusuf_ali: He was taught by one Mighty in Power,
5.shakir: The Lord of Mighty Power has taught him,
5.mohsin_khan: He has been taught (this Quran) by one mighty in power [Jibrael (Gabriel)].
5.arberry: taught him by one terrible in power,

6.sahih_international: One of soundness. And he rose to [his] true form
6.pickthall: One vigorous; and he grew clear to view
6.yusuf_ali: Endued with Wisdom: for he appeared (in stately form);
6.shakir: The Lord of Strength; so he attained completion,
6.mohsin_khan: Dhu Mirrah (free from any defect in body and mind), Fastawa [then he (Jibrael - Gabriel) rose and became stable]. [Tafsir At-Tabari].

7.sahih_international: While he was in the higher [part of the] horizon.
7.pickthall: When he was on the uppermost horizon.
7.yusuf_ali: While he was in the highest part of the horizon:
7.shakir: And he is in the highest part of the horizon.
7.muhammad_sarwar: the strong one who appeared on the uppermost horizon.
7.mohsin_khan: While he [Jibrael (Gabriel)] was in the highest part of the horizon,

8.pickthall: Then he drew nigh and came down
8.yusuf_ali: Then he approached and came closer,
8.shakir: Then he drew near, then he bowed
8.muhammad_sarwar: He (Gabriel) then came nearer and nearer.
8.mohsin_khan: Then he [Jibrael (Gabriel)] approached and came closer,
8.arberry: then drew near and suspended hung,

9.sahih_international: And was at a distance of two bow lengths or nearer.
9.pickthall: Till he was (distant) two bows' length or even nearer,
9.yusuf_ali: And was at a distance of but two bow-lengths or (even) nearer;
9.shakir: So he was the measure of two bows or closer still.
9.muhammad_sarwar: until he was as close to him as the distance of two bows, or even less.
9.mohsin_khan: And was at a distance of two bows' length or (even) nearer,
9.arberry: two bows' length away, or nearer,

10.sahih_international: And he revealed to His Servant what he revealed.
10.pickthall: And He revealed unto His slave that which He revealed.
10.yusuf_ali: So did (Allah) convey the inspiration to His Servant- (conveyed) what He (meant) to convey.
10.shakir: And He revealed to His servant what He revealed.
10.muhammad_sarwar: He revealed to God's servant whatever he wanted.
10.mohsin_khan: So did (Allah) convey the Inspiration to His slave [Muhammad SAW through Jibrael (Gabriel)].
10.arberry: then revealed to his servant that he revealed.

11.sahih_international: The heart did not lie [about] what it saw.
11.pickthall: The heart lied not (in seeing) what it saw.
11.yusuf_ali: The (Prophet's) (mind and) heart in no way falsified that which he saw.
11.shakir: The heart was not untrue in (making him see) what he saw.
11.muhammad_sarwar: His (Muhammad's) heart did not lie to him about what his eyes had seen.
11.mohsin_khan: The (Prophet's) heart lied not (in seeing) what he (Muhammad SAW) saw.
11.arberry: His heart lies not of what he saw;

12.sahih_international: So will you dispute with him over what he saw?
12.pickthall: Will ye then dispute with him concerning what he seeth?
12.yusuf_ali: Will ye then dispute with him concerning what he saw?
12.shakir: What! do you then dispute with him as to what he saw?
12.muhammad_sarwar: Will you then argue with him about what he saw?
12.mohsin_khan: Will you then dispute with him (Muhammad SAW) about what he saw [during the Mi'raj: (Ascent of the Prophet SAW over the seven heavens)].
12.arberry: what, will you dispute with him what he sees?

13.sahih_international: And he certainly saw him in another descent
13.pickthall: And verily he saw him yet another time
13.yusuf_ali: For indeed he saw him at a second descent,
13.shakir: And certainly he saw him in another descent,
13.muhammad_sarwar: He certainly saw him (Gabriel) during his other ascent
13.mohsin_khan: And indeed he (Muhammad SAW) saw him [Jibrael (Gabriel)] at a second descent (i.e. another time).
13.arberry: Indeed, he saw him another time

14.sahih_international: At the Lote Tree of the Utmost Boundary -
14.pickthall: By the lote-tree of the utmost boundary,
14.yusuf_ali: Near the Lote-tree beyond which none may pass:
14.muhammad_sarwar: to the Lot-tree (in the seven heavens)
14.mohsin_khan: Near Sidrat-ul-Muntaha [lote-tree of the utmost boundary (beyond which none can pass)],
14.arberry: by the Lote-Tree of the Boundary

15.sahih_international: Near it is the Garden of Refuge -
15.pickthall: Nigh unto which is the Garden of Abode.
15.yusuf_ali: Near it is the Garden of Abode.
15.shakir: Near which is the garden, the place to be resorted to.
15.mohsin_khan: Near it is the Paradise of Abode.
15.arberry: nigh which is the Garden of the Refuge,

16.sahih_international: When there covered the Lote Tree that which covered [it].
16.pickthall: When that which shroudeth did enshroud the lote-tree,
16.yusuf_ali: Behold, the Lote-tree was shrouded (in mystery unspeakable!)
16.shakir: When that which covers covered the lote-tree;
16.muhammad_sarwar: When the tree was covered with a covering,
16.mohsin_khan: When that covered the lote-tree which did cover it!
16.arberry: when there covered the Lote-Tree that which covered;

17.sahih_international: The sight [of the Prophet] did not swerve, nor did it transgress [its limit].
17.pickthall: The eye turned not aside nor yet was overbold.
17.yusuf_ali: (His) sight never swerved, nor did it go wrong!
17.shakir: The eye did not turn aside, nor did it exceed the limit.
17.muhammad_sarwar: (Muhammad's) eyes did not deceive him, nor did they lead him to falsehood.
17.mohsin_khan: The sight (of Prophet Muhammad SAW) turned not aside (right or left), nor it transgressed beyond (the) limit (ordained for it).
17.arberry: his eye swerved not; nor swept astray.

18.sahih_international: He certainly saw of the greatest signs of his Lord.
18.pickthall: Verily he saw one of the greater revelations of his Lord.
18.yusuf_ali: For truly did he see, of the Signs of his Lord, the Greatest!
18.shakir: Certainly he saw of the greatest signs of his Lord.
18.muhammad_sarwar: He certainly saw the greatest (signs) of the existence of his Lord.
18.mohsin_khan: Indeed he (Muhammad SAW) did see, of the Greatest Signs, of his Lord (Allah).
18.arberry: Indeed, he saw one of the greatest signs of his Lord.

19.sahih_international: So have you considered al-Lat and al-'Uzza?
19.pickthall: Have ye thought upon Al-Lat and Al-'Uzza
19.shakir: Have you then considered the Lat and the Uzza,
19.muhammad_sarwar: (Can anything as such be considered true) of al-Lat, al-Uzza,
19.mohsin_khan: Have you then considered Al-Lat, and Al-'Uzza (two idols of the pagan Arabs).
19.arberry: Have you considered El-Lat and El-'Uzza

20.sahih_international: And Manat, the third - the other one?
20.pickthall: And Manat, the third, the other?
20.shakir: And Manat, the third, the last?
20.muhammad_sarwar: and your third idol al-Manat (whom you considered as God's daughters)?
20.mohsin_khan: And Manat (another idol of the pagan Arabs), the other third?
20.arberry: and Manat the third, the other?

21.sahih_international: Is the male for you and for Him the female?
21.pickthall: Are yours the males and His the females?
21.yusuf_ali: What! for you the male sex, and for Him, the female?
21.shakir: What! for you the males and for Him the females!
21.muhammad_sarwar: Do sons belong to you and daughters to God?
21.mohsin_khan: Is it for you the males and for Him the females?
21.arberry: What, have you males, and He females?

22.sahih_international: That, then, is an unjust division.
22.pickthall: That indeed were an unfair division!
22.yusuf_ali: Behold, such would be indeed a division most unfair!
22.shakir: This indeed is an unjust division!
22.mohsin_khan: That indeed is a division most unfair!
22.arberry: That were indeed an unjust division.

23.sahih_international: They are not but [mere] names you have named them - you and your forefathers - for which Allah has sent down no authority. They follow not except assumption and what [their] souls desire, and there has already come to them from their Lord guidance.
23.pickthall: They are but names which ye have named, ye and your fathers, for which Allah hath revealed no warrant. They follow but a guess and that which (they) themselves desire. And now the guidance from their Lord hath come unto them.
23.yusuf_ali: These are nothing but names which ye have devised,- ye and your fathers,- for which Allah has sent down no authority (whatever). They follow nothing but conjecture and what their own souls desire!- Even though there has already come to them Guidance from their Lord!
23.shakir: They are naught but names which you have named, you and your fathers; Allah has not sent for them any authority. They follow naught but conjecture and the low desires which (their) souls incline to; and certainly the guidance has come to them from their Lord.
23.muhammad_sarwar: These are only names given by yourselves and your fathers. God has not given them any authority. They, (unbelievers), only follow mere conjecture and the desires of their souls, even though guidance has already come to them from their Lord.
23.mohsin_khan: They are but names which you have named, you and your fathers, for which Allah has sent down no authority. They follow but a guess and that which they themselves desire, whereas there has surely come to them the Guidance from their Lord!
23.arberry: They are naught but names yourselves have named, and your fathers; God has sent down no authority touching them. They follow only surmise, and what the souls desire; and yet guidance has come to them from their Lord.

24.sahih_international: Or is there for man whatever he wishes?
24.pickthall: Or shall man have what he coveteth?
24.yusuf_ali: Nay, shall man have (just) anything he hankers after?
24.shakir: Or shall man have what he wishes?
24.muhammad_sarwar: Can the human being have whatever he wishes?
24.mohsin_khan: Or shall man have what he wishes?
24.arberry: Or shall man have whatever he fancies?

25.sahih_international: Rather, to Allah belongs the Hereafter and the first [life].
25.pickthall: But unto Allah belongeth the after (life), and the former.
25.yusuf_ali: But it is to Allah that the End and the Beginning (of all things) belong.
25.shakir: Nay! for Allah is the hereafter and the former (life).
25.muhammad_sarwar: All that is in the life to come and all that is in this life belongs only to God.
25.mohsin_khan: But to Allah belongs the last (Hereafter) and the first (the world).
25.arberry: And to God belongs the First and the Last.

26.sahih_international: And how many angels there are in the heavens whose intercession will not avail at all except [only] after Allah has permitted [it] to whom He wills and approves.
26.pickthall: And how many angels are in the heavens whose intercession availeth naught save after Allah giveth leave to whom He chooseth and accepteth.
26.yusuf_ali: How many-so-ever be the angels in the heavens, their intercession will avail nothing except after Allah has given leave for whom He pleases and that he is acceptable to Him.
26.shakir: And how many an angel is there in the heavens whose intercession does not avail at all except after Allah has given permission to whom He pleases and chooses.
26.muhammad_sarwar: There are many angels in the heavens whose intercession will be of no benefit unless God grants such permission to whichever of them He wants.
26.mohsin_khan: And there are many angels in the heavens, whose intercession will avail nothing except after Allah has given leave for whom He wills and pleases.
26.arberry: How many an angel there is in the heavens whose intercession avails not anything, save after that God gives leave to whomsoever He wills and is well-pleased.

27.sahih_international: Indeed, those who do not believe in the Hereafter name the angels female names,
27.pickthall: Lo! it is those who disbelieve in the Hereafter who name the angels with the names of females.
27.yusuf_ali: Those who believe not in the Hereafter, name the angels with female names.
27.shakir: Most surely they who do not believe in the hereafter name the angels with female names.
27.muhammad_sarwar: Only those who do not believe in the life hereafter call the angels, females. They have no knowledge about it.
27.mohsin_khan: Verily, those who believe not in the Hereafter, name the angels with female names.
27.arberry: Those who do not believe in the world to come name the angels with the names of females.

28.sahih_international: And they have thereof no knowledge. They follow not except assumption, and indeed, assumption avails not against the truth at all.
28.pickthall: And they have no knowledge thereof. They follow but a guess, and lo! a guess can never take the place of the truth.
28.yusuf_ali: But they have no knowledge therein. They follow nothing but conjecture; and conjecture avails nothing against Truth.
28.shakir: And they have no knowledge of it; they do not follow anything but conjecture, and surely conjecture does not avail against the truth at all.
28.muhammad_sarwar: They only follow mere conjecture which can never sufficiently replace the Truth.
28.mohsin_khan: While they have no knowledge thereof. They follow but a guess, and verily, guess is no substitute for the truth.
28.arberry: They have not any knowledge thereof; they follow only surmise, and surmise avails naught against truth.

29.sahih_international: So turn away from whoever turns his back on Our message and desires not except the worldly life.
29.pickthall: Then withdraw (O Muhammad) from him who fleeth from Our remembrance and desireth but the life of the world.
29.yusuf_ali: Therefore shun those who turn away from Our Message and desire nothing but the life of this world.
29.shakir: Therefore turn aside from him who turns his back upon Our reminder and does not desire anything but this world's life.
29.muhammad_sarwar: (Muhammad), stay away from those who turn away from Our guidance and who do not desire anything except the worldly life.
29.mohsin_khan: Therefore withdraw (O Muhammad SAW) from him who turns away from Our Reminder (this Quran) and desires nothing but the life of this world.
29.arberry: So turn thou from him who turns away from Our Remembrance, and desires only the present life.

30.sahih_international: That is their sum of knowledge. Indeed, your Lord is most knowing of who strays from His way, and He is most knowing of who is guided.
30.pickthall: Such is their sum of knowledge. Lo! thy Lord is Best Aware of him who strayeth, and He is Best Aware of him whom goeth right.
30.yusuf_ali: That is as far as knowledge will reach them. Verily thy Lord knoweth best those who stray from His Path, and He knoweth best those who receive guidance.
30.shakir: That is their goal of knowledge; surely your Lord knows best him who goes astray from His path and He knows best him who follows the right direction.
30.muhammad_sarwar: This is what the extent of their knowledge amounts to. Your Lord knows best who has gone astray from His path and who has been rightly guided.
30.mohsin_khan: That is what they could reach of knowledge. Verily, your Lord it is He Who knows best him who goes astray from His Path, and He knows best him who receives guidance.
30.arberry: That is their attainment of knowledge. Surely thy Lord knows very well those who have gone astray from His way, and He knows very well those who are guided.

31.sahih_international: And to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth - that He may recompense those who do evil with [the penalty of] what they have done and recompense those who do good with the best [reward] -
31.pickthall: And unto Allah belongeth whatsoever is in the heavens and whatsoever is in the earth, that He may reward those who do evil with that which they have done, and reward those who do good with goodness.
31.yusuf_ali: Yea, to Allah belongs all that is in the heavens and on earth: so that He rewards those who do evil, according to their deeds, and He rewards those who do good, with what is best.
31.shakir: And Allah's is what is in the heavens and what is in the earth, that He may reward those who do evil according to what they do, and (that) He may reward those who do good with goodness.
31.muhammad_sarwar: To God belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth. In the end God will re-compense the evil doers for their deeds and reward the righteous ones for their deeds.
31.mohsin_khan: And to Allah belongs all that is in the heavens and all that is in the earth, that He may requite those who do evil with that which they have done (i.e. punish them in Hell), and reward those who do good, with what is best (i.e. Paradise).
31.arberry: To God belongs whatsoever is in the heavens and whatsoever is in the earth, that He may recompense those who do evil for what they have done, and recompense those who have done good with the reward most fair.

32.sahih_international: Those who avoid the major sins and immoralities, only [committing] slight ones. Indeed, your Lord is vast in forgiveness. He was most knowing of you when He produced you from the earth and when you were fetuses in the wombs of your mothers. So do not claim yourselves to be pure; He is most knowing of who fears Him.
32.pickthall: Those who avoid enormities of sin and abominations, save the unwilled offences - (for them) lo! thy Lord is of vast mercy. He is Best Aware of you (from the time) when He created you from the earth, and when ye were hidden in the bellies of your mothers. Therefor ascribe not purity unto yourselves. He is Best Aware of him who wardeth off (evil).
32.yusuf_ali: Those who avoid great sins and shameful deeds, only (falling into) small faults,- verily thy Lord is ample in forgiveness. He knows you well when He brings you out of the earth, And when ye are hidden in your mothers' wombs. Therefore justify not yourselves: He knows best who it is that guards against evil.
32.shakir: Those who keep aloof from the great sins and the indecencies but the passing idea; surely your Lord is liberal in forgiving. He knows you best when He brings you forth from the earth and when you are embryos in the wombs of your mothers; therefore do not attribute purity to your souls; He knows him best who guards (against evil).
32.muhammad_sarwar: Those who stay away from grave sins and indecency (should know that) for their trivial sins your Lord's forgiveness is vast. He knows best about you. When He created you from the earth and when you were embryos in your mother's wombs. Do not consider yourselves very great. God knows best who is the most righteous person.
32.mohsin_khan: Those who avoid great sins (see the Quran, Verses: 6:152, 153) and Al-Fawahish (illegal sexual intercourse, etc.) except the small faults, verily, your Lord is of vast forgiveness. He knows you well when He created you from the earth (Adam), and when you were fetuses in your mothers' wombs. So ascribe not purity to yourselves. He knows best him who fears Allah and keep his duty to Him [i.e. those who are Al-Muttaqun (pious - see V. 2:2)].
32.arberry: Those who avoid the heinous sins and indecencies, save lesser offences surely thy Lord is wide in His forgiveness. Very well He knows you, when He produced you from the earth, and when you were yet unborn in your mothers' wombs; therefore hold not yourselves purified; God knows very well him who is godfearing.

33.sahih_international: Have you seen the one who turned away
33.pickthall: Didst thou (O Muhammad) observe him who turned away,
33.yusuf_ali: Seest thou one who turns back,
33.shakir: Have you then seen him who turns his back?
33.muhammad_sarwar: (Muhammad), have you ever seen the one who has turned away (from guidance),
33.mohsin_khan: Did you (O Muhammad SAW) observe him who turned away (from Islam).
33.arberry: Hast thou considered him who turns his back

34.sahih_international: And gave a little and [then] refrained?
34.pickthall: And gave a little, then was grudging?
34.yusuf_ali: Gives a little, then hardens (his heart)?
34.shakir: And gives a little and (then) withholds.
34.muhammad_sarwar: and grudgingly spends very little for the cause of God?
34.mohsin_khan: And gave a little, then stopped (giving)?
34.arberry: and gives a little, and then grudgingly?

35.sahih_international: Does he have knowledge of the unseen, so he sees?
35.pickthall: Hath he knowledge of the Unseen so that he seeth?
35.yusuf_ali: What! Has he knowledge of the Unseen so that he can see?
35.shakir: Has he the knowledge of the unseen so that he can see?
35.muhammad_sarwar: Does he possess the knowledge of the unseen, thus, he sees (all things)?
35.mohsin_khan: Is with him the knowledge of the unseen so that he sees?
35.arberry: Does he possess the knowledge of the Unseen, and therefore he sees?

36.sahih_international: Or has he not been informed of what was in the scriptures of Moses
36.pickthall: Or hath he not had news of what is in the books of Moses
36.yusuf_ali: Nay, is he not acquainted with what is in the Books of Moses-
36.shakir: Or, has he not been informed of what is in the scriptures of Musa?
36.muhammad_sarwar: Has not he been informed of the contents of the Book of Moses
36.mohsin_khan: Or is he not informed with what is in the Pages (Scripture) of Musa (Moses),
36.arberry: Or has he not been told of what is in the scrolls of Moses,

37.pickthall: And Abraham who paid his debt:
37.yusuf_ali: And of Abraham who fulfilled his engagements?-
37.muhammad_sarwar: and about Abraham who fulfilled his duty (to God)?
37.mohsin_khan: And of Ibrahim (Abraham) who fulfilled (or conveyed) all that (what Allah ordered him to do or convey),
37.arberry: and Abraham, he who paid his debt in full?

38.sahih_international: That no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another
38.pickthall: That no laden one shall bear another's load,
38.yusuf_ali: Namely, that no bearer of burdens can bear the burden of another;
38.shakir: That no bearer of burden shall bear the burden of another-
38.muhammad_sarwar: Certainly no one will bear the responsibility of the sins of another,
38.mohsin_khan: That no burdened person (with sins) shall bear the burden (sins) of another.
38.arberry: That no soul laden bears the load of another,

39.sahih_international: And that there is not for man except that [good] for which he strives
39.pickthall: And that man hath only that for which he maketh effort,
39.yusuf_ali: That man can have nothing but what he strives for;
39.shakir: And that man shall have nothing but what he strives for-
39.muhammad_sarwar: nor can man achieve anything without hard labor.
39.mohsin_khan: And that man can have nothing but what he does (good or bad).
39.arberry: and that a man shall have to his account only as he has laboured,

40.sahih_international: And that his effort is going to be seen -
40.pickthall: And that his effort will be seen.
40.yusuf_ali: That (the fruit of) his striving will soon come in sight:
40.shakir: And that his striving shall soon be seen-
40.muhammad_sarwar: He will certainly see the result of his labor
40.mohsin_khan: And that his deeds will be seen,
40.arberry: and that his labouring shall surely be seen,

41.sahih_international: Then he will be recompensed for it with the fullest recompense
41.pickthall: And afterward he will be repaid for it with fullest payment;
41.yusuf_ali: Then will he be rewarded with a reward complete;
41.shakir: Then shall he be rewarded for it with the fullest reward-
41.muhammad_sarwar: and will be fully recompensed for his deeds.
41.mohsin_khan: Then he will be recompensed with a full and the best recompense.
41.arberry: then he shall be recompensed for it with the fullest recompense,

42.sahih_international: And that to your Lord is the finality
42.pickthall: And that thy Lord, He is the goal;
42.yusuf_ali: That to thy Lord is the final Goal;
42.shakir: And that to your Lord is the goal-
42.muhammad_sarwar: To your Lord will all things eventually return.
42.mohsin_khan: And that to your Lord (Allah) is the End (Return of everything).
42.arberry: and that the final end is unto thy Lord,

43.sahih_international: And that it is He who makes [one] laugh and weep
43.pickthall: And that He it is who maketh laugh, and maketh weep,
43.yusuf_ali: That it is He Who granteth Laughter and Tears;
43.shakir: And that He it is Who makes (men) laugh and makes (them) weep;
43.muhammad_sarwar: It is He who causes laughter and weeping.
43.mohsin_khan: And that it is He (Allah) Who makes (whom He wills) laugh, and makes (whom He wills) weep;
43.arberry: and that it is He who makes to laugh, and that makes to weep,

44.sahih_international: And that it is He who causes death and gives life
44.pickthall: And that He it is Who giveth death and giveth life;
44.yusuf_ali: That it is He Who granteth Death and Life;
44.shakir: And that He it is Who causes death and gives life-
44.muhammad_sarwar: It is He who causes death and gives life.
44.mohsin_khan: And that it is He (Allah) Who causes death and gives life;
44.arberry: and that it is He who makes to die, and that makes to live,

45.sahih_international: And that He creates the two mates - the male and female -
45.pickthall: And that He createth the two spouses, the male and the female,
45.yusuf_ali: That He did create in pairs,- male and female,
45.shakir: And that He created pairs, the male and the female
45.muhammad_sarwar: It is He who has created spouses, male and female,
45.mohsin_khan: And that He (Allah) creates the pairs, male and female,
45.arberry: and that He Himself created the two kinds, male and female,

46.sahih_international: From a sperm-drop when it is emitted
46.pickthall: From a drop (of seed) when it is poured forth;
46.yusuf_ali: From a seed when lodged (in its place);
46.shakir: From the small seed when it is adapted
46.mohsin_khan: From Nutfah (drops of semen male and female discharges) when it is emitted;
46.arberry: of a sperm-drop, when it was cast forth,

47.sahih_international: And that [incumbent] upon Him is the next creation
47.pickthall: And that He hath ordained the second bringing forth;
47.yusuf_ali: That He hath promised a Second Creation (Raising of the Dead);
47.shakir: And that on Him is the bringing forth a second time;
47.muhammad_sarwar: and on Him depends the life hereafter.
47.mohsin_khan: And that upon Him (Allah) is another bringing forth (Resurrection);
47.arberry: and that upon Him rests the second growth,

48.sahih_international: And that it is He who enriches and suffices
48.pickthall: And that He it is Who enricheth and contenteth;
48.yusuf_ali: That it is He Who giveth wealth and satisfaction;
48.shakir: And that He it is Who enriches and gives to hold;
48.muhammad_sarwar: It is He who grants people temporary and durable wealth.
48.mohsin_khan: And that it is He (Allah) Who gives much or a little (or gives wealth and contentment),
48.arberry: and that it is He who gives wealth and riches,

49.sahih_international: And that it is He who is the Lord of Sirius
49.pickthall: And that He it is Who is the Lord of Sirius;
49.yusuf_ali: That He is the Lord of Sirius (the Mighty Star);
49.shakir: And that He is the Lord of the Sirius;
49.muhammad_sarwar: It is He who is the Lord of Sirius.
49.mohsin_khan: And that He (Allah) is the Lord of Sirius (the star which the pagan Arabs used to worship);
49.arberry: and that it is He who is the Lord of Sirius,

50.sahih_international: And that He destroyed the first [people of] 'Aad
50.pickthall: And that He destroyed the former (tribe of) A'ad,
50.yusuf_ali: And that it is He Who destroyed the (powerful) ancient 'Ad (people),
50.shakir: And that He did destroy the Ad of old
50.muhammad_sarwar: It is He who utterly destroyed the ancient tribes of Ad,
50.mohsin_khan: And that it is He (Allah) Who destroyed the former 'Ad (people),
50.arberry: and that He destroyed Ad, the ancient,

51.sahih_international: And Thamud - and He did not spare [them] -
51.pickthall: And (the tribe of) Thamud He spared not;
51.yusuf_ali: And the Thamud nor gave them a lease of perpetual life.
51.shakir: And Samood, so He spared not
51.mohsin_khan: And Thamud (people). He spared none of them.
51.arberry: and Thamood, and He did not spare them,

52.sahih_international: And the people of Noah before. Indeed, it was they who were [even] more unjust and oppressing.
52.pickthall: And the folk of Noah aforetime, Lo! they were more unjust and more rebellious;
52.yusuf_ali: And before them, the people of Noah, for that they were (all) most unjust and most insolent transgressors,
52.shakir: And the people of Nuh before; surely they were most unjust and inordinate;
52.muhammad_sarwar: and the people of Noah; they were the most unjust and rebellious people.
52.mohsin_khan: And the people of Nuh (Noah) aforetime, verily, they were more unjust and more rebellious and transgressing [in disobeying Allah and His Messenger Nuh (Noah)].
52.arberry: and the people of Noah before -- certainly they did exceeding evil, and were insolent

53.sahih_international: And the overturned towns He hurled down
53.yusuf_ali: And He destroyed the Overthrown Cities (of Sodom and Gomorrah).
53.shakir: And the overthrown cities did He overthrow,
53.muhammad_sarwar: It is He who turned upside down the people of Lot
53.mohsin_khan: And He destroyed the overthrown cities [of Sodom to which Prophet Lout (Lot) was sent].
53.arberry: and the Subverted City He also overthrew,

54.sahih_international: And covered them by that which He covered.
54.pickthall: So that there covered them that which did cover.
54.yusuf_ali: So that (ruins unknown) have covered them up.
54.shakir: So there covered them that which covered.
54.mohsin_khan: So there covered them that which did cover (i.e. torment with stones).
54.arberry: so that there covered it that which covered.

55.sahih_international: Then which of the favors of your Lord do you doubt?
55.pickthall: Concerning which then, of the bounties of thy Lord, canst thou dispute?
55.yusuf_ali: Then which of the gifts of thy Lord, (O man,) wilt thou dispute about?
55.shakir: Which of your Lord's benefits will you then dispute about?
55.muhammad_sarwar: About which of the bounties of your Lord can they persistently dispute?
55.mohsin_khan: Then which of the Graces of your Lord (O man!) will you doubt.
55.arberry: Then which of thy Lord's bounties disputest thou?

56.sahih_international: This [Prophet] is a warner like the former warners.
56.pickthall: This is a warner of the warners of old.
56.yusuf_ali: This is a Warner, of the (series of) Warners of old!
56.shakir: This is a warner of the warners of old.
56.muhammad_sarwar: This is a (Prophet) like that of the ancient warners (Prophets).
56.mohsin_khan: This (Muhammad SAW) is a warner (Messenger) of the (series of) warners (Messengers) of old.
56.arberry: This is a warner, of the warners of old.

57.muhammad_sarwar: The Day of Judgment is drawing nearer.
57.mohsin_khan: The Day of Resurrection draws near,

58.sahih_international: Of it, [from those] besides Allah, there is no remover.
58.pickthall: None beside Allah can disclose it.
58.yusuf_ali: No (soul) but Allah can lay it bare.
58.shakir: There shall be none besides Allah to remove it.
58.muhammad_sarwar: No one besides God can rescue a soul from hardship.
58.mohsin_khan: None besides Allah can avert it, (or advance it, or delay it).
58.arberry: apart from God none can disclose it.

59.sahih_international: Then at this statement do you wonder?
59.pickthall: Marvel ye then at this statement,
59.yusuf_ali: Do ye then wonder at this recital?
59.shakir: Do you then wonder at this announcement?
59.muhammad_sarwar: Does this statement seem strange to them
59.mohsin_khan: Do you then wonder at this recital (the Quran)?
59.arberry: Do you then marvel at this discourse,

60.sahih_international: And you laugh and do not weep
60.yusuf_ali: And will ye laugh and not weep,-
60.shakir: And will you laugh and not weep?
60.muhammad_sarwar: and do they laugh instead of weeping,
60.mohsin_khan: And you laugh at it and weep not,
60.arberry: and do you laugh, and do you not weep,

61.shakir: While you are indulging in varieties.
61.mohsin_khan: Wasting your (precious) lifetime in pastime and amusements (singing, etc.).

62.sahih_international: So prostrate to Allah and worship [Him].
62.pickthall: Rather prostrate yourselves before Allah and serve Him.
62.yusuf_ali: But fall ye down in prostration to Allah, and adore (Him)!
62.shakir: So make obeisance to Allah and serve (Him).
62.muhammad_sarwar: So prostrate yourselves before God and worship him.
62.mohsin_khan: So fall you down in prostration to Allah, and worship Him (Alone).
62.arberry: So bow yourselves before God, and serve Him!
